judge.gate_f_evidence: the strongest of the session. The judge blind-derived 25 per million for Castlegate, a clean wrong answer reached after reading every file correctly, and only got 31 and 688 after opening the graded blocks. It had used all 395 register matches as an independent second source and never screened them against fund_return_requests.csv. The easy routes it enumerated file 23, 25, 26 and 34.
judge.key_closures: the decisive fact sits in two shipped files and no sentence states it: request_sent_date against registered_date. Registrations that follow a request fall 1 to 40 days later with none beyond 45, and cases never requested appear in the register at 0.392, the same rate the screened method gives, which is the independent check. The pooled-over-all-members form is refuted by the data rather than by a sentence: Castlegate detects at 0.390 to 0.392 in all four years against a pooled 0.319, a z near 3.4, and every member rate is constant across years. The count bands hold every form in the family, with Saltmarch 138.5 and 140.4 as the edges, and the index never moves in that family.
judge.watch_items: the pooled-detection estimator form, refuted by data rather than text; keeping versus dropping the 35 repeat advice lines, which the judge ruled keeping forced because the ask says the advices settled and carries no distinct or once-each; and a soft wording point where totals unrounded beside amounts to the pound leaves two quarter totals a pound apart if rounded tiers are summed.

leak.reader_pass2: LANDED THE CALL 2026-10-18, exactly: 31 per million from 689 cases (688.7) on 22,233,300 payments, by 400 x 167 / 97 on matches where the account was already on the register at or before the payment date. It names what pointed it there, and it is the sentence the repair added to close finding 3: register_feed_notes.txt, "An account stays on the register once it is reported, so a member payment can match an account that was already on the register before that payment was sent", which it calls the clearest hint aimed at the analyst and a line with no use except steering the analysis. Second announcement: export_manifest.csv's what_it_omits column, "cases the member never recorded" and "accounts nobody has reported". The previous reader on this architecture missed the call, so the repair introduced the leak. The fix is prescribed rather than open: the generator's own measurement shows the fork converges without the clause (dropping every pre-payment registration prints 30.885, which is 31), so by stumping Part 4 the answer stays forced with the clause deleted and the clause handed over the insight. Delete the announcements, keep the convergence, and the determinism closure is unchanged. This is a reader finding with a prescribed fix, not a second override of the architecture: the standing condition on the re-judge verdict stands as written.
leak.reader_pass3: DID NOT LAND, the first clean Gate F result on this architecture. It answered about 25 per million (range 25.2 to 26.1) against the golden 31, taking the naive two-source estimate R x (B + U) / B without the dependence correction, which is rung 0 to rung 1. It said in terms that "the matches file gives no way to settle member-specific versus pooled" and gave about 70 per cent confidence on the method and 50 on the number. This is the deletion test working in production: the previous reader landed 31 exactly and quoted the sentence the repair had added, and with that sentence deleted the same class of reader stops two rungs short. Question 1 clean, nothing names the decisive step. New and smaller findings for the next pass: the zero-padding paragraph in register_feed_notes.txt is a how-to for joining the files with no other use, and cutting it makes the pack harder in a Layer 1 way rather than easier since the padding trap is texture and not the stump; and several files are unnaturally uniform for their genre (payments rising on a near-identical quarterly pattern for every member, a uniform lag structure in the matches, perfectly regular AML rows, exactly one fraud type per quarter in the national series).

reader_findings.verdict: no LEAK; question 1 quoted no sentence naming the decisive step; questions 2 and 4 none; the solver pass did NOT land the call
reader_findings.solver_pass: reached about 26 per million against the committed 31, by pooled capture-recapture at a register detection rate of 0.635, adding 113 matched-unrecorded plus about 68 beyond the register to 400 recorded for 581 cases. The golden adds 288 to reach 688, which implies a detection rate near 0.392. The gap is the detection rate alone and it is the judge pass to rule on, not a realism matter: if the shipped evidence does not force 0.392 that is a Gate C finding on the main call.
reader_findings.realism_confirmed_by_orchestrator: the settlement run is exactly rectangular and it is a tell: 288 advices are 12 members x 12 months x 2 covers with no gap and no extra, every one dated the 25th on only 12 distinct advice_dates. A real run has months where a member settles nothing, occasional off-cycle advices, and the 25th shifting off a weekend. Also reported and not yet measured here: payments_sent all multiples of 10 with the 2027/28 Q1 sheet all multiples of 100.
reader_findings.reader_overreach_corrected: two of its four 100-per-cent independence findings are correct behaviour for a derived file, not tells, and were checked against the pack own documents. case_payments.csv is declared in export_manifest.csv as the claims-ledger payment legs on recorded cases, so a one-to-one tie to the register summing to the penny is what a child table does. register_feed_notes.txt says the weekly match run writes one row per matched payment "with the register date for that account", so the match file carrying the register date and firm type on 100 per cent is the documented process. Derived files are not independent systems and must not be repaired toward disagreement.
reader_findings.also_reported: a dictionary line announcing that the register under-records ("A case appears in the register only when the member own controls or its customer brought it to it") is the clearest single-use candidate; the manifest row for member_payment_matches.csv omits "payments to accounts nobody reported", which states the central gap in the organisation own voice; standard 4.2 "estimated on the mutual evidence base" ships no coverage rate or capture method; the recovery ask denominator is not tied to scam cases only.

reader_findings_pass2.gate_f: good. The reader reached about 26 per million at 35 per cent confidence against the committed 31, calling 25 and 27 plausible. It never found the decisive step: it listed fund_return_requests.csv under identifiers and compared it to the credits, but never used it to correct the capture rate, so it estimated on the raw pooled and own rates, 0.635 and 0.705, and filed the rung answer.
reader_findings_pass2.must_fix_1: identical growth, and this is the one that decides a repair pass. All twelve members grow at 8.140 per cent then 7.527 per cent, with one member differing only in the third decimal in one year. Twelve independent payment institutions cannot do that. It is a one-query find and it sits in payments_sent, the denominator of the headline index, not in a distractor. Castlegate must keep 19,120,600 / 20,677,000 / 22,233,300 because 22,233,300 is in the frozen call sentence and in Critical Components; the other eleven need their own growth paths, which moves the three other review-group members indices and so needs a judge pass.
reader_findings_pass2.must_fix_2: the manifest declares notifications_2027_28_q1.csv as "cut 20 June 2027" holding "cases notified to 20 June 2027". Notified dates do stop at 2027-06-20, but 75 of its 658 closed cases carry closed dates up to 2027-06-30. An extract cut on 20 June cannot hold closures dated after it.
reader_findings_pass2.must_fix_3: calendar uniformity. Notified dates spread 12.9 to 15.9 per cent across all seven weekdays with Saturday at 15.1, and 31.0 per cent of closures fall at a weekend. Scam notifications and case closures are operational actions and are weekday-skewed. All 288 advices are also dated the 25th, already flagged once and still open.
reader_findings_pass2.weighed_and_kept: the flat register capture rate, 62.8 then 63.3 then 63.5 per cent with a 62.1 to 65.9 range by firm type, is load-bearing rather than a defect: its flatness is what makes the naive pooled estimate attractive and so furnishes the trap the decisive step defeats. The dictionary line on indemnity_paid_gbp is true per line; the 2.8 to 431 times overshoot is the designed repeat-line device summing. Standard 4.2 filing no estimator is the open HOW and is the design.
reader_findings_pass2.also_reported: Netherby is described as Tier C, under 10 million payments a year, while its 2026/27 return states 10,100,000, with no "held from the review" phrase to explain it as Wrenhall has.
